company_notes:
Account background:
- Mid-market product analytics SaaS; main product: in-app product intelligence and recommendations for e-commerce customers.
- Current ML stack: embeddings on FAISS (self-hosted), some rule-based reranking. Want to replace with LLM-backed rerank + chat support.
Hosted API POC summary:
- Ran 2-week POC on Hosted API using 'rw-7b' variant. Traffic profile simulated: 25 qps peak, average 8 qps.
- Observed median latency (hosted): 160ms token-level, end-to-end chat median ~280ms for 512-token prompts.
- Cost: Hosted API per-token spend projected to ~$18k/month at current test load. High cost sensitivity; target <= $7k/month.
Cost optimization workshop (notes):
- Workshop attendees: AE Maya, SE Ravi, Product lead Jenna Ortiz, Infra lead Marco Li.
- Topics covered: dynamic batching strategies, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles (8-bit vs 4-bit), model routing/fallback (rw-7b -> rw-3b), and unit-economics model.
- Key outcomes: recommended caching front-door for repeated help-queries; expect 30-45% token reduction with prefix caching + 15-25% latency improvement with batching for 50ms batching window.
- Quantization experiments: 8-bit quantization produced negligible quality loss on 200 eval prompts; 4-bit showed slight drop in reranking fidelity on edge cases. SE recommends 8-bit quant profile for initial Dedicated rollout.
- Unit economics: Redwood Optimize model indicates Dedicated committed capacity reduces per-token infra cost by ~55-65% at 100k tokens/day commit. Break-even vs Hosted predicted at ~7 months given their traffic projection and expected growth.
POC technical asks and constraints:
- Must support SSO (SAML) and log-forwarding to customer's Splunk tenant.
- Data residency: primary US with EU shard for EU customers. Legal asks for retention controls and deletion API.
- Throughput SLO: sustain 50 concurrent inference sessions with p95 latency <= 350ms for 512 tokens.
- Failover: want cross-region fallback to avoid outages during promotions.
Sales/pricing notes:
- Procurement wants a two-tier pricing scenario: 12-mo committed Dedicated (preferred) vs pay-as-you-go Hosted with committed discount. Need term sheet for both.
- They asked explicitly: "If Dedicated gives us 60% cost savings, what are the up-front commit numbers and what SLA applies to burst capacity?"
Next steps (choppy action items):
- Send Dedicated sizing spreadsheet + updated pricing (Maya) by 2026-03-12.
- Legal: share Redwood SOC2 + data residency appendix (Ravi).
- Schedule 2-week Dedicated staging POC for May; confirm staging infra and test plan.
- Run 1-day quantization quality sweep on customer's reranking eval set (SE to run, report by 2026-03-20).
Concise quotes from contacts:
- Jenna (Product): "We need predictable unit-economics — can't have costs spike during a sale."
- Marco (Infra): "If we can get 50% cost reduction and SAML + logs, Dedicated becomes a no-brainer."
Additional context:
- Competitor risk: they are evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI for Hosted; Redwood advantage: clear Dedicated path + focused cost workshop.
- Internal sentiment: strong technical buy-in; procurement/legal are the gating factors.
